messages:
karen: fyi - ACME (tenant acme-inc) filing repeat p99 latency + auth failures since ~08:12 UTC. Customer sees lots of 503/429s, and their traffic is mostly short chat requests. Repro steps below. Can we triage fast? :rotating_light:

josh: on it. do you have any sample logs or request ids?

karen: paste from their support payload: `request_id=acme_20260315_8a3f`, `tenant=acme-inc`, `route=/v1/generate`, 503s and header `x-admit-wait-ms: 1200` showing queue delay. stack trace from their side: `ERR: request_timed_out after 1500ms`

lee: seeing matching spikes in our ingress metrics for tenant acme-inc at 08:11-08:18. per-tenant in-flight jumped to 750 (limit is 200). admission queue depth for the route hit ~18k. p95/p99 token latencies climb accordingly.

josh: 18k queue depth... that explains the p99. any auth errors?

karen: customer reported intermittent 401s too. Their token rotation happened at 08:10 (per their note). 401s correlate with spike but some 401s continue even after rotation.

lee: could be two simultaneous issues: rapid token rotation causing auth retries + our admission backlog causing auth timeouts. When KV cache pressure is high, our auth validation path takes longer. Check auth-service logs for latency for acme-inc.

josh: grabbing auth logs. snippet: ```yaml
auth/validate tenant=acme-inc lat_ms=3200 ok=false reason=token_fetch_timeout
auth/validate tenant=acme-inc lat_ms=480 ok=true
```

josh: token_fetch_timeout entries line up with the highest queue times. Looks like auth downstream (introspect) timed out under heavy load leading to 401s, then clients retried -> more queue pressure.

karen: customer wants mitigations now. They can't go offline. suggested options?

lee: immediate mitigations (fast):
- temporarily move acme-inc traffic to Dedicated pool (if available) or a less loaded region.
- increase tenant concurrency limit for acme-inc to allow more in-flight while we stabilize (tradeoff: could increase CPU use).
- enable fast-fail on auth validation path for short requests so we return 503 quickly rather than piling into queue.

josh: I can do a temporary tenant concurrency bump and enable fast-fail for `/v1/generate` for 30m. also can set routing rule to send acme-inc to dedicated if tenant has reserved capacity.

karen: customer prefers dedicated routing. they have reserved capacity on dedicated-east as of last month. please reroute.

josh: starting reroute now: `rhctl route add --tenant acme-inc --pool dedicated-east --weight 100`

deploy-bot: deploy started by josh: routing-rule/update for tenant acme-inc -> dedicated-east

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded (id: dr-9823) in 32s

josh: reroute applied. also bumped concurrency: `rhctl tenant update acme-inc --concurrency 600` and toggled auth fast-fail flag for short requests.

lee: monitoring telemetry: queue depth for acme-inc decreasing, in-flight now ~580, admit wait ms down from 1200->40. auth timeouts falling. p99 token latency trending down.

sara: customer reported reduced errors and confirms latency improved from ~3s to ~120-200ms. Thank you. :tada:

karen: leaving this open for 2h to monitor, will revert concurrency bump after stable and follow up with postmortem. ACTIONS:
- josh: rollback routing/concurrency after 2h or when p99 stable.
- lee: capture postmortem with root cause (auth timeout + tenant surge) and recommend hard limits / early fast-fail thresholds.
- k: send customer summary and ask for any further repro traces.

josh: noted. I'll also add a circuit-breaker on auth introspect path to avoid cascading timeouts.

lee: +1 on circuit-breaker; engineering ticket ENG-4932 to cover long-term fixes (rate-based admission, per-tenant surge protection, better auth caching).

karen: ack. closing once metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
